rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE GOVERNANCE AND MANAGEMENT OF THE PHILIPPINE SCIENCE HIGH SCHOOL SYSTEM, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Expanded Philippine Science High School System Act
rows.abstract:
Seeks to strengthen the governance and management of the Philippine Science High School (PSHS) System by expanding its scope and operations to different provinces in the Philippines.
Empowers the PSHS System Board of Trustees to approve policies and guidelines necessary in the establishment and operation of science high schools under the PSHS System to maintain the quality and uniform educational standard in all PSHS campuses.
Creates a Trust Fund to be used for priority programs and activities of the PSHS System.
Provides a PSHS System STEM curriculum from Grades 7 to 10 and Grades 11 to 12 which shall be recognized as Junior High School and Senior High School levels, respectively.
rows.status: Transmitted to the President on 2025-09-03

rows.title_short: Institutionalizing The Shared Service Facilities Project For Micro, Small, And Medium Enterprises, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 6977, As Amended, Otherwise Known As The " Magna Carta For Micro, Small And Medium Enterprises"
rows.abstract:
Aims to introduce government interventions to elevate and upscale the products being sold and exported by the country by institutionalizing the Shared Service Facilities (SSFs) project of the Department of Trade and Industry.
Creates additional SSF-Fabrication Labs (SSF-Fab Labs) in every province in order to encourage and assist our MSMEs in adopting new and innovative technologies in the manufacturing process which should improve the quality of the products as well as its market reach.

rows.author: K127;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE FULL AND EFFECTIVE IMPLEMENTATION AND ENFORCEMENT OF INTERNATIONAL MARITIME INSTRUMENTS OF WHICH THE PHILIPPINES IS A STATE PARTY
rows.abstract:
Defines the term “domestication” as used in this Act, among others.

Aims to address the risk faced by the country´s overseas shipping fleet being detained by other port states brought about by the government´s inability to fully and effectively implement international maritime instruments that the Philippines have ratified or acceded to. This contributes to the steady decline in the number of the country´s overseas shipping fleet.

Provides that among these instruments are the mandatory conventions involving safety of life at sea (SOLAS 1974 and its Protocol); prevention of pollution from ships (MARPOL); load lines (LL 66 and its 1988 Protocol); tonnage measurement of ships (Tonnage 1969); and regulations preventing collisions at sea (COLREG 1972).
rows.alias_name: “International Maritime Instruments Domestication Act of the Philippines”

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLES 333 AND 344, AND REPEALING ARTICLE 334, OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, ELIMINATING GENDER BIAS IN ADULTERY AND CONCUBINAGE
rows.abstract:
Proposes that Art. 333 of the Code be read as follows:Â  “MARITAL INFIDELITY is committed by any married PERSON who shall have sexual RELATIONS with a PERSON OTHER THAN HIS or her SPOUSE, and by the SEXUAL PARTNER of the MARRIED PERSON knowing the LATTER to be married, even if the marriage be subsequently declared void.”

“MARITAL INFIDELITY shall be punished by prision correccional in its medium and maximum periods.” . . .

Provides for several instances when any person accused shall be exempt from criminal liability or the penalty next lower in degree than that generally provided shall be imposed, with the same penalty on the co-accused in the marital infidelity case.

Proposes that Art. 344 replace the words adultery and concubinage with the word MARITAL INFIDELITY.

rows.abstract:
Proposes to amend Sections 6, 7, 8, 9 and 12 in the present law with the following provisions: the duration of the Doctor of Medicine degree will be at least 6 years, including the 1-year internship; enhancement of admission requirements without prejudice to the establishment of national eligibility examinations for medicine for admission to the MD degree; doing away with the requirement of reciprocity by resorting to the guiding principles and pillars of the WTO-GATS, other relevant international agreements, and mutual recognition arrangements being practiced globally.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATION OF COMMUNITY FUND POOLING OR PALUWAGAN GROUPS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract:
Aims to regulate the paluwagan system by creating an independent agency to be known as the Community Paluwagan Administration which shall prescribe rules and regulations for the creation and registration of paluwagan, and shall exercise the power of supervision over registered paluwagans.
Creates the Paluwagan Insurance Fund which aims to protect members of insured paluwagan in case of cessation of business.

rows.author: C102;
rows.title_full: CONSUMER DATA RIGHTS ACT OF 2024
rows.abstract:
Provides that the term “consumer data” encompasses financial and transactional data related to a consumer, whether recorded in a material form or not, that are collected, processed, and stored by data holders.

Aims to address the evolving challenges posed by the increasing reliance on consumer data in our digital economy and ensures the establishment of a set of standards that guarantee consumer protection and benefits regardless of the data source.

Aims to establish a comprehensive framework that fosters an environment of trust, transparency, and responsible data handling practices and intends to encourage competition and innovation among service providers, which is expected to drive improvements in products and services.

Proposes to create an inter-agency and multi-sectoral Consumer Data Rights Commission (CDRC); to establish accountability mechanisms, including an accreditation process for data recipients that will be allowed to receive consumer data directly from other data holders with the consumer´s express informed consent.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2024-01-22

rows.abstract:
"Neurodivergent People's Rights Act"
Defines several related terms:
“Ableism refers to the explicit and/or implicit systems of discrimination that give a person negative evaluations and inferior status on the basis of their disability and/or neurodivergent identity, while simultaneously privileging able-bodied or neurotypical people.”
States that “All persons with neurodevelopmental disabilities shall be treated as Persons with Disability in accordance with the provisions of RA 7277".
Proposes to include in the PWD Registry Form of the DOH several conditions to be classified as neurodevelopmental disabilities as follows:
1. Autism Spectrum Disorder 2. Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder 3. Down Syndrome 4. Cerebral Palsy 5. Global Developmental Delay 6. Intellectual Disabilities 7. Learning Disabilities 8. Motor Disorders 9. Communication Disorders l0. Other Neurodevelopmental Disorder.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A FRAMEWORK FOR CIRCULAR ECONOMY TO PROMOTE
SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION AND CONSUMPTION, AND NATIONAL ECONOMIC SECURITY
rows.abstract:
Intends to address the country´s lagging behind in terms of environmental sustainability based on the latest ranking on performance indicators on ecosystem vitality (e.g. biodiversity, water resources), environmental health (e.g. air quality, waste management), and climate change.
Proposes an economic paradigm shift for a sustainable development that balance the needs of the environment and the economy through transition to circular economy.  Defines circular economy as an economic model of creating value by extending product lifespan through improved design and servicing, and relocating ways from the end of the supply chain to the beginning.  This intends to efficiently utilize resources by its continual use, and aims to retain the highest utility and value of products components and materials at all times, through sharing, leasing, reuse, repair, refurbishment, and recycling in an almost closed loop.
Describes embracing circularity through reimagining how we design, produce, and consume goods; creating products that are durable, repairable, and ultimately recyclable, to minimize waste, reduce raw material extraction, and foster regeneration in both natural and human-made ecosystems.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ENHANCING PHILIPPINE TAX INCENTIVES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 27, 28, 112, 292, 293, 294, 295, 296, 297, 300, 301, 309, 310 AND 311, AND ADDING A NEW SECTION 295-A IN THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE OF 1997, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Enhancing Philippine Tax Incentives, Amending For The Purpose Sections 27, 28, 112, 292, 293, 294, 295, 296, 297, 300, 301, 309, 310 And 311, And Adding A New Section 295-a In The National Internal Revenue Code Of 1997, As Amended, And For Other Purposes ( C R E A T E     M O R E )
rows.abstract: Seeks to reconcile disparities between the Corporate Recovery and Tax Incentives for Enterprises (CREATE) Act and its implementing rules and regulations. Aims to a.) Improve the equity and efficiency of the corporate tax system by lowering the rate, widening the tax base, and reducing tax distortions and leakages; b.) Develop a more responsive and globally competitive tax incentives regime that is performance-based, targeted, time-bound, and transparent, and can be customized to optimize economic opportunities and trends; c.) Provide support to business in their recovery from unforeseen events such as outbreak of communicable diseases or a global pandemic, and strengthen the nation´s capability for similar circumstances in the future; and d.) Create a simpler, fairer, and more equitable tax system that will allow for inclusive growth and generation of jobs and opportunities in all the regions of the country, and ensure access and ease in the grant of these incentives especially for applicants in least developed areas.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 240, ON ELECTIONS RESULTING IN TIE, OF BATAS
PAMBANSA BLG. 881, AS AMENDED ALSO KNOWN AS THE OMNIBUS ELECTION CODE
OF 1985
rows.abstract:
Intends to do away with the practice of coin tossing/drawing of lots as tie-breakers in  election cases resulting on a tie by transmitting the FINAL RESULTS TO THE SANGGUNIAN CONCERNED. . . SHALL HOLD A SPECIAL SESSION THREE DAYS AFTER RECEIVING THE TRANSMITTAL FROM THE BOARD OF CANVASERS at which the SANGGUNIAN shall BREAK THE TIE BY A MAJORITY VOTE and shall proclaim as elected the candidate who WILL be CHOSE BY THE VOTE OF A MAJORITY OF ALL MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIAN, . . .
. . . FOR DISTRICT REPRESENTATIVE OR DISTRICT SANGGUNIAN MEMBER, ONLY THE MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIAN OF THAT DISTRICT WILL BE ALLOWED TO VOTE.
IN CASES OF SENATORS, THE DULY ELECTED 23 SENATORS WILL VOTE AMONG THEMSELVES ON WHO WIL BE THE LAST SENATOR WHO WILL COMPLETE THEIR ROSTER.

rows.author: K114;
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE MEDICINE VOUCHER PROGRAM AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Seeks to address the long-standing problem of accessing medicines that are not available in government hospitals and formularies of the Government - establishes a mechanism for the accreditation of private pharmacies/health care medicine providers to ensure the availability of a wide range of essential/uncommon/quality medicines necessary for the treatment of all Filipinos (indigent individuals and families; informal sector workers; indigenous people and other vulnerable groups).
Tasks the Philippine National Formulary under the DOH to administer the Medicine Voucher Program and provides safeguards to prevent fraud, abuse, and corruption in its administration.
